why: Counting sort when values are small: with only the values 0, 1 and 2, count how many of each there are, then overwrite the array with that many 0s, 1s and 2s. Two linear passes, no comparisons.
hints: A comparison sort is O(n log n). How many different values can appear?
Only three. If you know how many 0s, 1s and 2s there are, you know the sorted array.
Count in one pass, then write count[0] zeros, count[1] ones, count[2] twos back into nums. O(n), O(1) extra. The one-pass follow-up is the Dutch national flag (three pointers).
pitfalls: Rearrange in place and return the same array.
